subtitles.text:
The human who looked into the distance
encountered something that resembled what was most intimate to them.

Researchers analyzing subtle distortions in light
from distant galaxies discovered a pattern that could not be explained
as a signal from any known celestial body or form of matter.

Later, instruments on Earth also detected a similar structure, which
showed a strong correlation with fluctuations in human emotion.

This discovery led emotions to be understood
not phenomena confined to an individual’s inner life,
but as forces that also leave traces in the spaces beyond the body.

Researchers called the field formed by emotions accumulating
and overlapping in space a “resonant field.”

However, it remained unclear if resonant fields were formed
solely by human emotions, if they were also influenced by other
beings, or how they related to the pattern discovered. in space.

Within resonant fields, different types of
unknown entities were repeatedly detected.

The entities could not be classified as any known biological species
and were presumed, perhaps, to have existed long before.

What they were and why they were drawn
to resonant fields remained unknown.

The detector measured changes occurring in space
and reconstructed emergent entity’s state from recurring patterns
within them, but what it actually looked like remained unknown.

As observations accumulated, the previously unstable
patterns of the emergent entities gradually began to show consistency.

When observations became less frequent or
the conditions of the resonant field changed,
the detected movement and repetition also changed.
The signal sometimes weakened or dispersed again.

Before the nature of these emergent entities had been
sufficiently understood, personal companion-entity
detectors and a companion app became widely available.
People began calling them “companion entities.”

The app translated the companion entities’ states
into terms people could understand.

The signal’s intensity, duration, distribution, and repetitiveness
were translated into the language of personality, mood, intimacy,
and attachment, and the unknown phenomena became a character
on the screen—one that people could discover and care for

People named their companion entities, recorded
changes in their conditions, and reached their
hands toward the points indicated by their detector.
These gestures held both tenderness and interference.

As companion entities became widespread,
the market expanded into real estate and various other services.

Companion entities were tied to the characteristics of
the resonant fields that accumulated in a place.

When registered users moved out of their homes, they could not detect
the same companion entity again in the new location.

Repeated detection records in a particular space became an indicator
of the likelihood that a companion entity would appear,
and the real estate market began promoting frequently detected
spaces as premium properties.

Resonant fields were converted into a measure of space’s value,
and companion entities became objects that individuals
could register and manage.

Companies provided subscription plans for storing
the observation records, interaction data,
and character models of companion entities.

The translations and record-keeping created
to understand unknown beings became both forms of care
and a means of ownership.
People came to realize that no space is ever completely empty.

Humans were already entangled with the resonances of other beings
and, regardless of a detector, no one could fully
escape those entanglements.

To recognize something was to alter
the conditions of its existence.
No one could place themselves outside the world.
People called this era “the end of solitude.”
